Steph — draft below that I think is defensible operationally. I kept it narrow to avoid promising full image handovers or customer-data exports.

---Draft schedule (for internal review)---
Turnkey Exit & Proof-of-Access Protocol (draft):
1) Trigger: Termination effective date as defined in the Order Form.
2) Deliverables (within 30 calendar days of trigger):
   - Environment snapshot manifest (checksums + metadata) describing VM/container images and deployed model artifacts (no raw customer data).
   - Signed HSM attestation confirming custody of keys used for the deployment (if HSM in scope).
   - Operator-access revocation report: audit listing active accounts/credentials removed and actions taken.
   - Access logs export covering the preceding 90 days (metadata only; excludes payload contents unless expressly requested and agreed).
3) Delivery method: Secure SFTP or mutually agreed physical transfer; envelope signed via DocuSign for chain-of-custody.
4) Warranty: Redwood warrants that deliverables will contain only operational metadata and artifacts necessary to verify continuity of service. Redwood will not deliver raw customer content unless explicitly requested in writing and with accompanying data transfer agreement.
5) Escrow-like option: If customer requires an escrow steward, Redwood will accept a recognized third-party escrow agent; Redwood will execute a limited-scope escrow agreement covering only binary artifacts and key attestations.

Open items for Legal: maximum liability tied to deliverables; definition of "environment snapshot"; whether logs export can include request/response payloads under any circumstance.

If this looks good, I'll convert to redline and return to Acme.

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Infrastructure Engineering, Redwood Inference

Claire — thanks for the clear ask and the template. Apologies for the short turn. We've reviewed internally and attached our proposed redlines (PDF) and a compact schedule (docx). Summary of changes:

- We accepted a 30 calendar day timeline for the curated deliverables listed below.
- We limited "environment snapshot" to manifests (checksums + images) and excluded raw customer payload unless Acme signs a separate data export agreement.
- We added a clause for HSM attestation when keys are customer-provisioned to avoid exposing Redwood-rooted key material.
- We proposed using a neutral escrow steward only for binary artifacts and attestations (not logs or payloads).
- We added an SLA for evidence-delivery communications (status check-ins at day 7/15/25).

Next steps: please review the attached redlines and the short schedule. If acceptable, legal can route DocuSign and we'll prepare the secure SFTP endpoint and chain-of-custody checklist. If Acme's counsel requires payload-level logs or raw datasets, we will need a signed DTA and an extension to the delivery timeline (we flagged 60 days for that scenario).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to hop on a 30-minute call to finalize.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
